author: Rhyma Castillo
title: Luby's president addresses viral claim about 'a man looking at little girls' in Houston area - NewsBreak
text:
By Rhyma Castillo ,
11 hours ago "Our priority remains the safety of our guests, the integrity of our team, and ensuring that all concerns are addressed responsibly, thoroughly, and with care," the Luby's president said in a statement. (Mike Sutter/Staff) Luby’s President Calvin Gin has addressed a viral social media video showing one Luby's employee making accusations about "a man looking at little girls" during an incident that reportedly took place in the Houston area.
"A video currently circulating online shows an altercation between a Luby’s employee and a manager," Gin wrote in a Tuesday statement.
"During the exchange, the employee can be heard making a statement about 'a man looking at little girls.' We recognize the seriousness of statements involving the safety of minors and understand how quickly concern can escalate when clips are shared without full context," he added.
ALSO READ: Camp Mystic health officer didn’t call 911 or alert nurses
In his statement, the Luby's president said company representatives are working to fully understand the events leading up to the incident, "including the statements made and the individuals referenced." (TOM REEL, STAFF / SAN ANTONIO EXPRESS-NEWS) The video has circulated across multiple social media platforms, including X , TikTok and Instagram . The video depicts an unidentified man in a black Luby's uniform expressing apparent frustration at his manager, accusing an unidentified individual of "predatorizing (sic) little girls" on multiple occasions.
In a phone call with the Express-News, a representative for Luby's stated the employee making accusations of misconduct was accusing an unidentified individual who was not present at the time the video was filmed, not the manager he was speaking to. In his statement, Gin said company representatives are working to fully understand the events leading up to the incident, "including the statements made and the individuals referenced."
From the parking lot of Luby's on Fredricksburg Road, the Jim’s sign up the street is visible on Wednesday, Aug. 28, 2024, in San Antonio, Texas. (Josie Norris/San Antonio Express-News) ALSO READ: Demolition underway for Antiquarian Book Mart on Broadway
Gin has asked the public to refrain from sharing unverified claims. A representative for Luby's could not confirm whether law enforcement has been involved in investigating the incident.
"Our priority remains the safety of our guests, the integrity of our team, and ensuring that all concerns are addressed responsibly, thoroughly, and with care," Gin said.
